output.scope_note: The paper is about moisture degradation of argyrodite sulfide solid electrolytes (Li6PS5Cl and Li5.5PS4.5Cl1.5) and reports their measured Li-ion conductivities in the main text.

records.synthesis_method: high-energy ball milling followed by annealing
records.evidence_quote: Specifically, Li5.5PS4.5Cl1.5 (Cl1.5) exhibits an ionic conductivity of 4.5 mS cm−1, compared with 2.3 mS cm−1 for Li6PS5Cl (Cl1.0)
records.evidence_location: Results, first paragraph of Introduction section (p. 4)
records.notes: Value is cited to Supplementary Fig. 1; the EIS temperature (298 K) and method come from the Methods EIS section, which describes the pellet measurements of the synthesized electrolytes. Conductivity is derived from total electrolyte resistance R, hence 'total'. Annealing at 550 °C is a crystallization step, not a sintering step, so sintering fields are null.
